name: client-first
status: proposal - not yet applied; v2 remains the active schema until the corpus is re-tagged
principle: Tag a document only with what varies BETWEEN documents. Anything constant per client moves to the client master and is joined at query time. Tagging cost is per document (millions); client attributes are per client (thousands).
rationale: v2 grew to 30 fields because it tried to be a legal-knowledge schema AND a client schema. Retrieval, however, always starts from a client question.

8 of the 30 fields were computable from the client record (country, pc_code, sector_agreement, coverage, service_line, visibility default, languages, sub_jurisdiction). They were being re-derived per document - the expensive place to do it.
5 more were precedence machinery (legal_basis, rule_level, precedence, bindingness, instrument) that collapses into one human-readable authority value.
Result: 30 -> 13 required tags, and the agent's judgment surface shrinks from ~10 fields to 4. Cheaper, faster, and far more consistent, because most remaining fields are deterministic or inherited.

states.*: applies to all clients / unscoped (positive wildcard)
states.null: not determinable - pipeline or human must fill

filter_rule: match(doc, q) = (doc.client_id intersects q.client_ids) OR doc.client_scope = 'generic'; then filter on validity, then order by authority
join_rule: country, pc_code/sector agreement, worker groups, coverage, team and language all resolve through the client master at query time

client_id.note: the anchor of the whole schema

applies_to_entity.required: when the client has more than one entity/country
applies_to_entity.note: replaces doc-level country: it is what keeps a BE instruction away from the client's NL payroll

doc_type.changed: v2 had 8; control/template/system fold into procedure/reference, which is how users actually ask for them

process_domain.changed: v2 had 17; input/time_attendance/implementation/year_end fold into the step they belong to, compliance/systems/reporting fold into governance/declarations

worker_category.note: kept as a DOC tag on purpose: it is the key that resolves which joint committee / sector agreement applies, and blue-vs-white collar rules differ materially in BE payroll

authority.note: replaces legal_basis.scheme + rule_level + precedence + bindingness. Precedence is derived from this order (most specific wins on conflict), never stored.

visibility.by: rule from client scope, agent may narrow

valid_to.by: rule, else null = still in force

last_reviewed.note: a document with no end date must carry a review date, otherwise 'is this still valid' is unanswerable

legal_ref.note: OPTIONAL free-form exact-match key: 'CAO 82', 'IDCC 1486', 'PC 124'. No enum, no validation - it exists so literal lookups stay possible without maintaining 17 schemes.

supersedes.note: lineage only; validity windows answer 'what was in force'

client_master.note: This is now half the schema. Maintained once per client, not once per document.

retrieval_model.query: What applies to client X for the May 2026 payroll run?
retrieval_model.plan: client_scope=per_client AND client_id=X  UNION  client_scope=generic; valid_from <= 2026-05-31 AND (valid_to is null OR valid_to >= 2026-05-01); order by authority (client_instruction > client_collective > sector_agreement > law > internal); join client master for country/committee context
client master lookup on entities.sector_agreement.code = 116 -> client_ids -> their documents. No document tagging needed for this: the sector lives on the client.

retrieval_model.query: What is new for client X this quarter?
retrieval_model.plan: client_id=X AND valid_from >= quarter start, all authorities, newest first

retrieval_model.query: Is this standard procedure still valid?
retrieval_model.plan: client_scope=generic AND client_id='*' AND last_reviewed older than the review threshold -> stale queue

retrieval_model.query: Can consultant Y send this to client X?
retrieval_model.plan: visibility in (all, client) AND (client_id=X OR client_scope=generic) AND servicing_team=Y

human: client_id when the document does not name a client
authority when the agent is under 0.7
valid_from when a law change has no date in the text

moved_to_client_master.pc_code: per entity / per worker group on the client

dropped_from_v2.legal_basis {scheme,id}: 17-value enum maintained per country -> replaced by authority (5) + optional free-form legal_ref
dropped_from_v2.rule_level: collapses into authority; the 8-level ladder was never used beyond 4 distinct values in practice
dropped_from_v2.precedence: derived from authority order at query time
dropped_from_v2.bindingness: folded into authority (a sector agreement IS binding; an internal procedure is binding on staff; the distinction the field drew was between legal force and internal force, which authority already encodes)
dropped_from_v2.pay_component: 36% fill; 20-value open vocab per country; process_domain already routes these questions
dropped_from_v2.output_channel: 25-value cross-country list; process_domain=declarations + legal_ref covers the real query shape ('DmfA for client X')
dropped_from_v2.sub_jurisdiction: never fired on the corpus (0%) and belongs to the client entity anyway
dropped_from_v2.source_system / uri: infrastructure metadata, kept outside the tag record
dropped_from_v2.version / translation_of / known_at: nice-to-have lineage; add back only if the demo needs them (supersedes is the one exception kept optional)

trade_offs: LOST: 'show me every document about holiday pay' across all clients - pay_component was the only field that could answer that. Acceptable if the demo question is client-first.

LOST: cross-country legal drill-down (IDCC vs PC vs CCNL comparison) - legal_ref keeps the literal code but the scheme is no longer machine-typed. Recoverable later by re-adding ONE optional {scheme, id} field.
GAINED: the agent judges 4 fields instead of ~10, so per-document cost and variance both drop; more fields are deterministic or inherited, so the review queue gets shorter and more targeted.
GAINED: a client's attributes are fixed once and reused by every document - a wrong PC code is corrected in one place instead of thousands.

migration.effort: one deterministic projection script over out/*.json; no re-inference needed for the dropped fields
